citation.authors: Ngandeu Schepanski S, Batta F, Schroter M, Ngoumou GB et al

record.population: 13 studies, 4,105 adults (cold showers, immersion, winter swimming)
record.design: Systematic review and meta-analysis of randomised, non-randomised and single-group studies of psychological outcomes
record.finding: Pooled estimates generally favoured cold exposure for depressive symptoms, perceived stress, wellbeing and mood, but confidence intervals were wide, several estimates shrank in controlled-only analyses, and most studies had serious or critical risk of bias. The authors state the evidence does not establish that cold-water exposure improves mood or stress and that it should not be regarded as a standalone psychological treatment. Anxiety showed little consistent benefit.
